gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2's '1,000 W solar input' is a single 12–60 V, 20 A input. BLUETTI's own SP200L kit panels are 24.6 V open-circuit, so at most two can be wired in series (49.2 V; three would be 73.8 V, over the 60 V limit). At the 20 A cap that limits the kit's panels to under 984 W however many you add, so the advertised 1,000 W can't be reached with them.
standout_why: I compared against powersized.com/solar-generator-kits (cited in all three chats) and theoutagebrief.com 2kWh shootout (cited). Powersized gives Elite 200 V2 as '1,000 W, 12–60 V, 20 A' and states the general rule that panels in series add their Voc and must stay under the maximum. Its only worked example is Jackery SolarSaga 200 W on the Explorer 1000 v2. It never applies the rule to the Elite 200 V2 with its own SP200L panels or to the 20 A current cap. Theoutagebrief gives only maximum solar watts per model (DELTA 2 Max 1,000 W, Explorer 2000 v2 400 W, AC200L 1,200 W, C2000 Gen 2 800 W), with no voltage, amps or wiring. I couldn't read unpluggedwatts.com (SSL certificate error). ChatGPT's own answers sell the Elite 200 V2 on 'up to 1,000W solar input' and 'future solar expansion' without this limit.
decides: It confirms the Elite 200 V2 + 2×200 W kit ($1,499 on BLUETTI's US store, 2026-11-08) as a good 400 W starter kit: two SP200L in series is 49.2 V Voc, inside the 60 V window. It also removes the 'expand to 1,000 W of solar' argument for buying it with SP200L panels: adding more SP200L panels can't reach 1,000 W. That argument needs panels with a higher operating voltage. A shopper who expects to grow solar past about 800–900 W should compare stations with two solar inputs (Powersized lists DELTA 2 Max as 2 × 500 W) or a wider voltage window (AC200L at 12–145 V per Powersized). The page should give this as a hard limit from BLUETTI's own figures, not as a test result.

findings.label: Solar (PV) input limit
findings.value: 1,000 W max, 12 V to 60 V, 20 A max
findings.note: Compare table: '1,000W Max., 12V to 60V, 20A Max.' FAQ Q1: 'PV input: Elite 200 V2: 12V-60V/20A, 1,000W max'. 1,000 W ÷ 20 A = 50 V, so the full rating needs the array to work at 50 V or more.

findings.label: Open-circuit voltage (Voc)
findings.note: Page says 'Open Circuit Voltage (OCV): 24.6V'. BLUETTI US store: $399 (compare-at $1,197), in stock, read with storecheck on 2026-11-08.

findings.label: Short-circuit current (Isc)
findings.note: Page says 'Short Circuit Current (Isc): 10.8A'. Two strings in parallel give 21.6 A Isc, just over the station's 20 A input limit, so a third parallel string adds nothing.

findings.label: Most SP200L panels in series on one input
findings.value: 2 panels (49.2 V Voc); 3 would be 73.8 V, over the 60 V maximum
findings.note: Arithmetic from BLUETTI's own figures: 24.6 V × 2 = 49.2 V, which is ≤ 60 V. 24.6 V × 3 = 73.8 V, which is > 60 V. Station limit is 12–60 V (elite-200-v2-2-sp200l page). Cold weather raises Voc, so two in series also leaves room for that.

findings.label: Most solar power possible with SP200L panels
findings.value: Under 984 W (a strict upper bound, so the 1,000 W rating is out of reach)
findings.note: Upper bound = longest legal string's Voc (49.2 V) × 20 A input cap = 984 W. A panel always works below its Voc, so real harvest is lower. I did not compute an operating-point figure because I couldn't open SP200L's Vmp on a maker page (see unsourced).

findings.label: Battery and AC output
findings.note: Page says '2,073.6Wh (54 Ah)' and '2,600W in total, 120V,21.6A'. In the box: AC charging cable, documentation, unit, grounding screw. No solar cables or series/parallel connectors are listed.
